article.story: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- — The mantra in New England's locker room under Mike Vrabel has been to never apologize for a win. So no one was feeling bad about the Patriots improving to 2-0 in the AFC East after their victory over the New York Jets on Sunday. They also know that mounting injuries will require much more from everyone if they want to keeping winning. Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, New England overcame losing three offensive linemen and Charles Woods came up with Geno Smith's first interception of the season in the fourth quarter to help the Patriots hold on for a 26-19 win. “It was sloppy. It wasn't clean,” said Maye, who completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards in his third consecutive game with at least three TD passes. “It wasn’t football that we felt like (was) complementary.” Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry had touchdown catches for the Patriots (4-2), winners of three in a row. Douglas had a team-high seven catches for 86 yards. A.J. Brown had three catches for 27 yards for the Patriots in his return from injured reserve, but his timing was off and he had three drops on his 10 total targets. “None of us were at our best today, but we were good enough,” Vrabel said. New England won its fourth straight against the Jets and 19th in its last 21 meetings despite right tackle Morgan Moses (ankle), left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and right guard Ben Brown (knee) leaving with injuries. “Those guys are playing through injuries,” Maye said. "We (had) three go down today, so these guys are fighting hard. They’re fighting their butts off, and it goes through them." The Jets (2-4) had a chance to tie it in the third quarter, but the Patriots held them to a field goal. New York squandered another opportunity to cut the deficit to a field goal in the fourth quarter when Smith was picked off by Woods. It came on Smith's 166th pass of the season, ending his longest opening stretch to a season without an interception. “Finishing on offense and detail on defense is something we’ve got to get better at because I think we gifted two touchdowns that shouldn’t have happened,” Jets coach Aaron Glenn said. Smith finished 20 of 30 for 252 yards a touchdown to rookie Omar Cooper Jr., who had six catches for 103 yards in his return from IR after missing four games with an ankle injury. New England's defense, which got a boost from cornerback Christian Gonzalez returning from a two-game absence with a shoulder injury, held New York to 0 for 3 in the red zone. The Jets were also 3 of 10 on third down and were stopped on fourth-down runs on consecutive possessions in the second quarter. “Those plays are huge for us. I’m just proud of the defense, how we stayed together," Gonzalez said. "They got some momentum there late and we were just able to finish the game.” Building the lead The Patriots led 17-3 at the half, courtesy of Doubs’ diving 42-yard touchdown catch and a 9-yard scoring grab by Douglas. The Jets trimmed the gap to 17-10 in the third quarter after Cooper got behind Patriots safety Craig Woodson and caught a 42-yard TD from Smith. That remained the score when Jets edge rusher David Bailey stripped TreVeyon Henderson of the ball and Jamien Sherwood recoverer at the New England 36. New York drove to 10, but Smith was sacked by Elijah Ponder, forcing the Jets to settle for a 36-yard field goal by Jason Sanders. The Patriots responded on their next series, capping a 12-play, 68-yard drive with a 7-yard TD strike from Maye to Henry, but Andy Borregales missed the extra point. Just four plays later and the Jets down 10, Smith overshot Kenyon Sadiq on a deep pass that was intercepted by Woods. Injuries Jets: LB Kiko Mauigoa left with a thigh injury in the first quarter. Patriots: Doubs (shoulder) exited in the first quarter following his touchdown catch and didn’t return. ... Moses favored his left ankle when he left early in the second quarter. ... Vera-Tucker left in the second with a hamstring injury and was ruled out. ... Brown had trouble putting weight on his left leg as he was helped off in the fourth quarter with a knee injury. Up next Jets: Host the Dolphins next Sunday. Patriots: Visit the Bears on Thursday night. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
